title: Indicator approximation and rotation sensitivity
statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in\mathbb R$. Write $u_\theta(x)=\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Then
\[\int\left|u_\theta(x)-1_A(x)\right|\,d\gamma_n(x)=\Pr\!\left(1_A(X)\ne 1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y)\right),\]
where $X,Y$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb R^n$.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. For independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$, put $R_A(\theta)=\Pr(1_A(X)\ne1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))$. If $A$ is measurable, then $\int|u_\theta(x)-1_A(x)|\,d\gamma_n(x)=R_A(\theta)$ for every real $\theta$.
